### IN FLIGHT — the api-capstone pair, and why it needed its own tool
firestore.rules and HubRegistry.js are a MATCHED PAIR (hub-registry-audit fails if they disagree)
in DIFFERENT deploy scopes, so they cannot ship atomically. Order is load-bearing:
  rules first  -> an id is briefly over-reserved. Chris confirmed by reading firestore.rules:839-870
                  that the reserved list appears exactly once, in `allow create`. No student path.
  hosting first-> the live registry would serve an id production rules do NOT reserve, which is the
                  exact shadowing the list exists to prevent.
Chris BLOCKED the checklist version: the smoke gate on the rules path is PROVABLY BLIND to rules
content (/firebase/i and /firestore/i are in IGNORED_ERROR_PATTERNS at smoke/run.js:219-220), and
hub-registry-audit runs only in deploy.sh. Worse, I had already built verify-deployed-rules.sh to
close that hole and left it out of the plan -- grep showed it was called from nowhere.
Now enforced in code: deploy-rules-pair.sh refuses to start unless the marker is ABSENT, deploys
rules, HARD-GATES on reading the LIVE ruleset from the Rules REST API, and only then ships hosting.
firestore:indexes dropped from scope -- clean vs HEAD but last changed 07-21 and I cannot confirm
that version was ever deployed.

### A VERIFIER THAT COULD NOT SUCCEED
verify-deployed-rules.sh interpolated the marker into a triple-quoted Python literal. 'api-capstone'
contains single quotes, so it ERRORED on both present and absent and printed MISMATCH either way --
which PASSES a "prove it can fail" test while detecting nothing. Marker now goes through the
environment; discriminates three ways, and Chris exercised it against production himself.
The 403 that first read as "releases: 0" was an ADC quota-project error my parser swallowed.
